scenarios.name: Base plan
scenarios.description: The 2027 plan as written, with both hiring requests.

scenarios.name: New business won, seniors leaving
scenarios.description: Retainers grow 20% from March, and designers leave at over twice the planned rate all year.

scenarios.name: Retainers +25%
scenarios.description: A good year on the retainer book, which is a capacity problem wearing a nice hat.

scenarios.name: Designers poached
scenarios.description: One team loses people at two and a half times the planned rate and no other team is touched.

scenarios.name: A client leaves in June
scenarios.description: Retainer work drops a fifth from June. The bench is now the problem.

scenarios.name: Hiring freeze
scenarios.description: Both requests are withdrawn. Nobody already here leaves because of it.

scenarios.name: Margin pressure
scenarios.description: The cost base has to come in 10% under plan.

scenarios.name: Tooling saves 12%
scenarios.description: The same work takes 12% fewer hours everywhere.

scenarios.name: Delivery risk +60%
scenarios.description: Every engagement is markedly likelier to miss.

scenarios.name: Squeeze with a hiring freeze
scenarios.description: Growing, losing people, and not allowed to replace them.

interventions.name: Put 22% of design production with freelancers
interventions.description: A trusted freelance bench takes the production work. Available within the month, and it costs roughly what the people would have.

interventions.name: Bring the design hires forward
interventions.description: Search fees and buying out notice periods. Two months becomes one.

interventions.name: Move 6 front-end engineers into design production
interventions.description: They can do production design inside a month. They are not doing Meridian while they do it.

interventions.name: Stop building our own design system
interventions.description: The internal investment. Nothing bills against it, and eleven people come back.

interventions.name: Take Brightline to 60% of scope
interventions.description: The identity and the core applications, not the long tail. A conversation with the client, and less of the fee.

interventions.name: Run Meridian leaner and longer
interventions.description: A smaller team over a longer run. It lands later, and the client has an opinion about that.

interventions.name: Defer the framework bid by 2 months
interventions.description: Push the bid out and give Strategy some air. Bids have dates, so check what this actually costs.

decisions.question: The Design Studio cannot hold both engagements.
decisions.setup: Brightline and Meridian both staff out of the same thirty-eight people, and the studio is also carrying the retainer book and an internal design system nobody bills for.

options.label: Put production with freelancers
options.why: A trusted bench takes 22% of the work inside a month, and costs roughly what the people would have.

options.label: Stop the internal design system
options.why: Eleven people come back to billable work. The thing that was going to make next year cheaper does not happen.

options.label: Hold and run hot
options.why: The studio absorbs it, as studios do, right up until people start leaving.

decisions.question: Two senior designers have resigned this month.
decisions.setup: Five design hires were approved in March at a two-month lead time. Seniority is not a number of people; the work they were holding does not redistribute evenly.

options.label: Bring the hires forward
options.why: Search fees and bought-out notice. Two months becomes one.

options.label: Move six engineers into production
options.why: They can do production design inside a month. They are not doing Meridian while they do it.

options.label: Backfill in the normal way
options.why: The hires land in May and the studio covers until then.

decisions.question: The framework bid and Brightline want the same fourteen people.
decisions.setup: Strategy is fourteen people. The bid is worth more than Brightline and is under half as likely to land.

options.label: Defer the bid two months
options.why: Give Strategy some air. Bids have submission dates, so check whether this changes the number at all.

options.label: Take Brightline to 60%
options.why: The identity and the core applications, not the long tail. Less work and less fee.

options.label: Run both at full scope
options.why: Everyone stays busy and something gives in August.

decisions.question: Meridian is the year, and it is tight.
decisions.setup: Twenty-three engineers on one client, against a book that grew 20% in March. Whatever else happens, this one has the biggest number attached to it.

options.label: Run Meridian leaner and longer
options.why: A smaller team over a longer run. It lands later, and the client has an opinion about that.

options.label: Move six engineers into production
options.why: If you have not already. It takes them off Meridian.

options.label: Hold the staffing
options.why: Meridian keeps its team and everything else works around it.

decisions.question: One more before the year closes.
decisions.setup: October. Whatever you have not spent is still there, and December is short.

options.label: Put production with freelancers
options.why: If you have not already. A month to mobilise means it is working for November and December.

options.label: Stop the internal design system
options.why: If you have not already. It is the only thing here nobody is paying for.

options.label: Take the year as it stands

demoIntent.summary: A client services firm where the constraint is a named group of senior people, the internal investment always loses to billable work, and winning new business is itself a capacity problem.
intents: Design is the constraint and it is seniority, not headcount.
The internal design system is the only work nobody is paying for, which makes it the easy cut and the expensive one.
Moving engineers into design helps the studio and takes them off the largest contract in the building.

routes.name: Support tickets that become engineering work
